I have resolved the issue in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-pxwemy8s/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1413) in [compiler.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-pxwemy8s/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py).

### Cause
When a query without joins or filters (such as `Model.objects.all()`) is passed to [`SQLDeleteCompiler`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-pxwemy8s/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407), `self.query.alias_map` is initially empty because [`Query.get_initial_alias()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-pxwemy8s/django/db/models/sql/query.py#L916-L926) has not yet been called. As a result, [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-pxwemy8s/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412) counted `0` active aliases and returned `False`, causing [`SQLDeleteCompiler.as_sql()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-pxwemy8s/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1423-L1440) to fall back to wrapping the deletion in an unnecessary `WHERE pk IN (SELECT pk FROM ...)` subquery.

### Fix
Call `self.query.get_initial_alias()` in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-pxwemy8s/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412) to ensure the base table is present in `alias_map` before counting active table aliases.
